newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish police block march of Uighur exiles.
newsitem.headline: Turkish police block march of Uighur exiles.

text.p: Police halted a march on the Chinese consulate in Istanbul on Sunday by Uighur exiles protesting at the killing of their ethnic kin during a riot in northwest China's Xinjiang province last week.

Several hundred demonstrators earlier held a rally about three kilometres (two miles) from the consulate waving nationalist flags and chanting anti-Chinese slogans, before attempting to march on the consulate, witnesses said.

"An end to Chinese oppression in East Turkestan," one banner read. Xinjiang province was known as the Republic of East Turkestan during a brief period of independence in the 1940's, before being taken over by Beijing after the revolution in 1949.

Hundreds of Turkish police in riot gear blocked the route of the march and scuffles broke with the demonstrators and eggs were thrown before the police successfully turned them away. No arrests were made.

Chinese authorities said about 1,000 people, mostly Uighur farmers or unemployed youths, rampaged through the town of Yining earlier this month, smashing and burning cars, looting shops and demanding China pull out of the mostly-Moslem province.

A statement from the group organising the Istanbul march, the Eastern Turkestan National Centre, said it had reports of summary executions carried about by Chinese authorities. Earlier, the group put the death toll at almost 90.
According to Chinese officials, nine people died and nearly 200 were wounded in the clashes.

Istanbul has traditionally been a centre of exile for Turkic-speaking Uighurs, where their cause attracts support from Pan-Turkist groups, seeking unification of Turkic-speaking countries from Turkey to Central Asia.
